mainTopic: Public vows, remarrying a wife divorced over a vow, a woman's extra blemishes, praise of ארץ ישראל, and who must prove when a bride's blemishes began
overview: This amud opens by asking how many people make a vow 'public', so that it cannot be released, as with the oath to the גבעונים. רב נחמן בר יצחק says three and רבי יצחק says ten. Next comes a משנה where רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר argue about remarrying a wife who was divorced over a vow. The גמרא explains that the real question is whether a husband is willing to have his wife embarrassed in בית דין. רבא then explains a ברייתא about a woman betrothed on condition that she has no vows. The גמרא challenges him, and the answer is that a woman is happy with almost any husband, which several sages show with popular sayings. The גמרא then lists blemishes that count in a woman but not in a כהן: sweat, bad breath, a hidden mole, a dog-bite scar, a deep voice, and unusual breasts. A short aggadic passage praises ארץ ישראל and those who go up to it. Finally, a new משנה begins on who must prove when a bride's blemishes started, and the view of the חכמים continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The oath to the גבעונים could not be undone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק about the oath to the גבעונים as its source that a vow made in front of many people cannot be released.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And the children of Israel did not strike them, because the leaders of the congregation had sworn to them."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק from ספר יהושע. It shows that the oath to the גבעונים stayed binding, even though they had tricked the Jews.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גבעונים fooled the Jews into swearing to them. Normally a mistaken oath can be released, yet the Jews still kept this one. This is the proof that an oath made in public (ברבים) cannot be undone.

keyTerms.meaning: The people of Givon, who tricked יהושע into making a treaty

phrases.english: "And the children of Israel did not smite them,
phrases.notes: יהושע 9:18

phrases.english: for the princes of the assembly had sworn to them."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא הִכּוּם בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל כִּי נִשְׁבְּעוּ לָהֶם נְשִׂיאֵי הָעֵדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of public vows from before this section of the daf.
steps.raayaObject: A vow made in front of many people cannot be released.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The oath to the גבעונים in יהושע 9:18, which stayed binding even though it was made by mistake.

steps.title: How many people count as 'many'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the minimum number of people is for a vow to count as made ברבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how many people count as 'many'?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know a public vow cannot be released, the גמרא asks how many people are needed to make it 'public.' This sets up two answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule depends on the vow being made 'in front of many.' That word needs a real number, so the גמרא asks for one.

phrases.english: And how many are 'many'?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכַמָּה רַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the exact definition of the term behind the rule just proven.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The minimum number of people that counts as רבים.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: three people
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says three people, learning it from the words 'many days' in the פסוק about a זבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: three. 'Days' means two, so 'many' days means three.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that three people are enough. He learns this from how the תורה uses the word רבים elsewhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plural word 'days' means at least two. Adding 'many' (רבים) pushes it one higher, to three. So the word רבים means three.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives the first answer
'Many days': the phrase used about a זבה
A woman who has an unusual flow of blood

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר: שְׁלֹשָׁה.
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: Three.
"Days" means two,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:25. The פסוק about a זבה says 'many days.'

phrases.english: "many" days means three.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר: שְׁלֹשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of how many people make up 'many.'
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Three, learned from 'ימים רבים' in the פסוק about a זבה.

steps.title: רבי יצחק: ten people
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק says ten, because the פסוק about the גבעונים uses the word עדה, and an עדה is ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: ten, because the word 'congregation' (עדה) is written about them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק gives a different answer: ten people. He reads it straight from the word עדה in the גבעונים פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן בר יצחק learns the number from a different topic (זבה). רבי יצחק learns it from the very פסוק that teaches the rule, where the leaders are called 'of the עדה.' An עדה is at least ten people.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives the second answer
A congregation; a group of at least ten

steps.whatToRemember: How many make a vow 'public'? רב נחמן בר יצחק says three (from 'ימים רבים'). רבי יצחק says ten (from the word עדה).

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzḥak said: Ten,
as "assembly" is written in relation to them.
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the leaders who swore to the גבעונים. An עדה is counted as at least ten people.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר: עֲשָׂרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, different answer to the same question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Ten, because the word עדה is used about the leaders who made the oath.

steps.title: The משנה: רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר on remarrying after a vow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה. רבי מאיר says a man who divorced his wife over a vow that needs a חכם may not remarry her. רבי אלעזר says the ban on that kind of vow is only because of a vow that does not need a חכם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: any vow that needs a חכם to look into it, he may not take her back. רבי אלעזר says: they only forbade the kind that needs a חכם because of the kind that doesn't.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a משנה about a man who divorced his wife because of her vow. The two תנאים argue about when he is not allowed to take her back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some vows can only be released by a חכם after he looks into them (חקירת חכם). Others the husband could cancel himself. רבי מאיר forbids remarriage for the חכם kind on its own merits. רבי אלעזר says the ban on that kind only exists as a backup to the other kind.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who argues with רבי מאיר here
A חכם's investigation, needed to release some vows
He may not take her back (remarry her)

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
Any vow that requires investigation by a halakhic authority,
he may not remarry her.
Rabbi Elazar says:
They prohibited the one that requires investigation
only due to the one that does not require it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: כׇּל נֶדֶר שֶׁצָּרִיךְ חֲקִירַת חָכָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: a משנה about remarrying a wife divorced over a vow.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: if the vow needs a חכם, he may not remarry her. רבי אלעזר: that ban exists only because of vows that don't need a חכם.

steps.title: What is the root of their disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what idea רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר really argue about.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the deeper reason behind the מחלוקת. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives the two rulings but not the reasoning. The גמרא wants to find the single idea that splits them.

phrases.english: With regard to what principle do they disagree?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the משנה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying principle that divides רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר.

steps.title: Is a husband willing to have his wife embarrassed in court?
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר holds that a man is willing to have his wife embarrassed in בית דין. רבי אלעזר holds that he is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר holds: a man is willing for his wife to be embarrassed in בית דין. רבי אלעזר holds: a man is not willing for his wife to be embarrassed in בית דין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the argument is about the husband's attitude. Would he be willing to have his wife go to בית דין to get her vow released?
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי מאיר, the husband would have taken her to a חכם. So he could later claim he divorced her by mistake, and he may not remarry her. According to רבי אלעזר, he would never put her through that embarrassment. So the חכם kind of vow is only forbidden as a backup to the other kind.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: a husband is willing to have his wife embarrassed in בית דין. רבי אלעזר: he is not.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir holds:

phrases.aramaic: אָדָם רוֹצֶה שֶׁתִּתְבַּזֶּה אִשְׁתּוֹ בְּבֵית דִּין,
phrases.english: a man is willing for his wife to be degraded in court,
Rabbi Elazar holds:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אָדָם רוֹצֶה שֶׁתִּתְבַּזֶּה אִשְׁתּוֹ בְּבֵית דִּין.
phrases.english: a man is not willing for his wife to be degraded in court.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר סָבַר: אָדָם רוֹצֶה שֶׁתִּתְבַּזֶּה אִשְׁתּוֹ בְּבֵית דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by naming the principle they disagree about.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They disagree about whether a husband is willing to have his wife embarrassed in בית דין.

steps.title: רבא: the ברייתא is about an important woman
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the ברייתא where the woman is not betrothed even after a חכם released her vow. She comes from an important family, and the husband wants the betrothal undone completely so he is not forbidden to her relatives.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Here we are dealing with an important woman, since he says: I do not want to be forbidden to her relatives.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to an earlier ברייתא. It said a woman betrothed on condition that she has no vows is not betrothed, even if a חכם later released her vow. רבא gives his own explanation of that ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the קידושין counted, even a later divorce would leave him forbidden to her close relatives, like her mother or sister. Since she is from an important family, he wants to keep the option of marrying into it. So he wants the קידושין to never have taken effect at all, and that is why she is not betrothed.

keyTerms.meaning: An important woman (from an important family)
It is not acceptable to me

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not explaining the רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר מחלוקת just before. He is going back to the earlier ברייתא about betrothing on condition that she has no vows.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Here we are dealing with an important woman,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the earlier ברייתא, where a חכם released her vow and she still is not betrothed.

phrases.english: as he says: It is not amenable to me
to be forbidden to her relatives.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: הָכָא בְּאִשָּׁה חֲשׁוּבָה עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the earlier ברייתא and offers a new explanation of it.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the case narrowly (אוקימתא): a woman from an important family.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Once a חכם releases her vow, the condition seems fulfilled and she should be betrothed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The husband wants the קידושין fully undone so he stays permitted to her relatives, so she is not betrothed.

steps.title: Challenge from the ברייתא's second half
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's second half says that if the man's vow is released or his blemish healed, she is betrothed. By רבא's logic, the ברייתא should have said she is not betrothed, because she might not want to be forbidden to his relatives.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, look at the second half, which teaches: But if he went to a חכם who released him, or to a doctor who healed him, she is betrothed. It should teach that she is not betrothed, and we should say this is an important man, since she says: I do not want to be forbidden to his relatives!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's explanation. It uses the second half of the same ברייתא, where the condition was about the man instead of the woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the second half, the man had vows or blemishes, and a חכם or doctor fixed them. There the ברייתא rules that she is betrothed. If רבא's reasoning were right, the ברייתא could have said the same about an important man, so she would not be betrothed. Since it didn't, רבא's explanation looks weak.

keyTerms.meaning: The latter clause of a teaching
Let it teach (it should have said)

phrases.english: If so, the latter clause, which teaches:

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הוּא שֶׁהָלַךְ אֵצֶל חָכָם וְהִתִּירוֹ,
phrases.english: But if he went to a halakhic authority and he dissolved his vow,
phrases.notes: Here the condition was that the man has no vows or blemishes, and he turned out to have them.

phrases.english: or to a doctor and he healed him, she is betrothed.
Let it teach that she is not betrothed,
and let us say that here we are dealing with an important person,
as she says: It is not amenable to me
to be forbidden to his relatives!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, סֵיפָא דְּקָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's explanation from the second half of the same ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's explanation that the case is about an important woman.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same reasoning should apply to an important man in the second half. The ברייתא's ruling there (she is betrothed) shows it did not think that way.

steps.title: A woman is happy with almost any husband
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a woman wants to be married at almost any cost, as ריש לקיש's saying shows, so she would not want the betrothal undone.
steps.simpleTranslation: She is content with any man at all, as ריש לקיש taught. ריש לקיש said that women say: 'It is better to live as two than to live alone like a widow.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 9. A woman is so eager to be married that she does not care about being forbidden to his relatives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 9 the גמרא asked why the woman would not also want the betrothal fully undone. The answer is that the man and the woman think differently. She would rather stay betrothed to a flawed man than be alone, so the ברייתא rightly says she is betrothed.

keyTerms.meaning: With anything at all, with whatever there is
It is fine for her, she is happy with it

steps.confusionAlert: These sayings describe how women were thought to feel. They explain a difference in what each side wants, not a law about who is allowed to marry.

phrases.english: She is content with anyone at all,
as taught by Reish Lakish.
For Reish Lakish said:
"It is better to live as two
phrases.notes: This is a popular saying that women would say about themselves.

phrases.english: than to live alone like a widow."

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיהִי בְּכׇל דְּהוּ נִיחָא לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes between what the man wants and what the woman wants
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The woman, like the man, would want the betrothal fully undone so she is not forbidden to his relatives
steps.terutzMaskana: The woman prefers any marriage to being alone, so she is happy for the betrothal to stand

steps.title: More sayings showing women prefer any husband
steps.stepSummary: אביי, רב פפא and רב אשי each give a saying showing that a woman is proud and content even with a lowly husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: A woman whose husband is as small as an ant still puts her chair among the noblewomen. רב פפא said: A woman whose husband is a wool comber calls him to sit with her at the doorway. רב אשי said: A woman whose husband is lowly does not even ask for lentils for her pot.
steps.whatsHappening: Three more sages add sayings that support the same idea as ריש לקיש. Being married at all makes a woman feel important.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each saying shows a woman who is proud of a husband with little worth: tiny, poor in his trade, or unable to feed her. This backs up the answer in step 10 that she would not want to undo the marriage.

keyTerms.meaning: An ant, meaning a very small, unimportant man
A wool comber, a lowly job

phrases.english: Abaye said:
One whose husband is as small as an ant
places her chair among the noblewomen.
Rav Pappa said: One whose husband is a wool comber
calls him to the doorway and sits with him.
Rav Ashi said: One whose husband is lowly
does not ask for lentils for her pot.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: דְּשׁוּמְשְׁמָנָא גַּבְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more sayings that support the answer in step 10
steps.raayaObject: The claim that a woman is happy with any husband
steps.raayaSupportSource: Popular sayings quoted by אביי, רב פפא and רב אשי

steps.title: A side remark about these women
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא remarks that these women with lowly husbands are unfaithful and claim the children are their husbands'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: And all of these women commit adultery and say the children belong to their husbands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a short teaching as a side remark about the women in the sayings just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This gives one more reason why such women want to be married: a husband gives cover for children from other men. It closes the discussion about the woman's attitude.

keyTerms.meaning: They hang it on, they blame it on

steps.whatToRemember: The man may want the betrothal fully undone, but the woman is happy to stay married. That is why the ברייתא says she is betrothed when his flaw goes away.

phrases.english: It was taught: And all of them commit adultery
phrases.notes: 'All of them' means the women with lowly husbands from the sayings above.

phrases.english: and say the children are their husbands'.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: וְכוּלָּן מְזַנּוֹת וְתוֹלוֹת בְּבַעְלֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a final remark about the women described in step 11
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The women in these sayings are unfaithful and claim the children are their husbands'.

steps.title: Three extra blemishes that count for women
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה: blemishes that disqualify כהנים also count for women. A ברייתא adds sweat, a mole, and bad breath for women.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: All blemishes that disqualify כהנים also count for women. It was taught: They added to these sweat, a mole, and bad breath.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes the משנה's rule about blemishes and brings a ברייתא that adds three more blemishes for women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a betrothal can be undone if the woman has a blemish that would disqualify a כהן. The ברייתא adds three more blemishes that are serious in a woman, which suggests they do not disqualify a כהן. The next step will challenge this.

phrases.english: All blemishes that disqualify, and so on.
phrases.notes: This quotes our משנה: blemishes that disqualify כהנים from serving also count as blemishes in a woman.

phrases.english: It was taught: They added to these
sweat, a mole, and bad breath.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל מוּמִין שֶׁפּוֹסְלִין וְכוּ׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Besides the blemishes of כהנים, sweat, a mole, and bad breath are also blemishes in a woman.

steps.title: Don't these blemishes disqualify כהנים too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: a משנה lists a filthy animal as blemished, and another משנה says animal blemishes also disqualify people, so sweat should disqualify a כהן too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do these not disqualify כהנים? But we learned: The old, the sick, and the filthy animal are blemished. And we learned: These blemishes, whether permanent or temporary, disqualify a person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ברייתא's idea that sweat counts only for women. It uses two משניות to show that sweat also disqualifies a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One משנה lists a filthy animal as unfit. A second משנה says the same blemishes, even temporary ones, disqualify a person, meaning a כהן. So filth and sweat should already be on the כהן list, and there would be no need to add them for women.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn in a משנה?

phrases.english: And do these not disqualify כהנים?
But we learned: The old, the sick, and the filthy.
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in בכורות about which animals are unfit.

phrases.english: And we learned: These blemishes,
whether permanent or temporary,
disqualify a person.
phrases.notes: A person here means a כהן.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָנֵי בְּכָהֲנֵי לָא פָּסְלִי? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא in step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that sweat is an extra blemish only for women
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משניות in בכורות make filthiness a blemish for animals and for כהנים, so sweat should already disqualify a כהן.

steps.title: Sweat that washes off versus sweat that stays
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא answers: the ברייתא means sweat that can be washed off, and the משנה means sweat that cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: This is not difficult. Here it means sweat that goes away. There it means sweat that does not go away.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא answers the challenge by showing the two sources are talking about different kinds of sweat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sweat that does not go away is a real blemish for a כהן, as the משנה says. Sweat that can be washed off does not disqualify a כהן, but it is still a blemish in a woman. So the ברייתא can add it for women only.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction

steps.whatToRemember: Sweat that cannot be removed disqualifies a כהן. Sweat that can be washed off does not disqualify a כהן, but it still counts as a blemish in a woman.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא, לָא קַשְׁיָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said: This is not difficult:
Here it means sweat that goes away,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the ברייתא, which adds sweat only for women.

phrases.english: there it means sweat that does not go away.
phrases.notes: 'There' means the משנה in בכורות, which treats it as a blemish for a כהן.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא, לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 14
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the cases: each source talks about a different kind of sweat
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All sweat disqualifies a כהן, so the ברייתא's addition makes no sense
steps.terutzMaskana: Only sweat that cannot be removed disqualifies a כהן. Sweat that can be washed off is a blemish only in a woman.

steps.title: Sweat is different from filth, and a כהן can cover it for a short time
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the challenge was wrong from the start. 'Filthy' means a lasting foul smell. A כהן can cover sweat with vinegar and bad breath with pepper long enough to do the עבודה, but a woman cannot do that all the time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Are you comparing sweat to filth? A כהן can get rid of sweat with wine vinegar for a while. He can also hold pepper in his mouth for bad breath and then do the עבודה. A woman cannot do this all the time.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a second answer to the challenge from Step 14. He says sweat and 'filthy' are two different things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that 'filthy' in the משנה includes sweat. רב אשי says 'filthy' means a smell that never goes away. Sweat and bad breath can be covered for a short time, and a כהן only needs a short time to do the עבודה. A wife lives with her husband all the time, so a short fix does not help her.

keyTerms.meaning: Sweat; here, a bad smell from sweat
Filthy; a smell that stays all the time
You are setting one source against another

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי is not saying sweat is fine for a woman. He is saying the opposite: a short-term fix is enough for a כהן's עבודה but not for married life, so sweat counts only for a woman.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Are you setting sweat against filth?
phrases.notes: The 'filthy' animal is from the משנה quoted in Step 14. רב אשי says that means a smell that never goes away.

phrases.english: There, regarding priests,
it is possible to remove it with wine vinegar.
And from bad breath too,
it is possible for him to hold pepper in his mouth
and perform the service.
But regarding a woman, it is not possible.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: זֵיעָה אַמְּזוֹהָם קָא רָמֵית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the challenge of Step 14, different from רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's answer in Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: a lasting smell versus a smell that can be covered for a while
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Sweat is the same as the 'filthy' blemish, so it should disqualify a כהן too.
steps.terutzMaskana: Filth is a lasting smell. Sweat and bad breath can be covered for a short time, which is enough for a כהן but not for a wife.

steps.title: What kind of mole counts only for a woman?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא listed a mole as a blemish for a woman and not for a כהן. The גמרא checks every kind of mole: with hair, large without hair, small without hair. Each kind seems to get the same ruling for both.
steps.simpleTranslation: What kind of mole is this? If it has hair, it disqualifies both a woman and a כהן. If it has no hair and is large, it disqualifies both. If it is small, it disqualifies neither.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the mole in the ברייתא from Step 13. It asks what case is meant, since no kind of mole seems to work only for a woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said a mole is a blemish only for a woman. The גמרא goes through all the options and finds that each one gives the same answer for women and כהנים. So the ברייתא's difference seems to have no case.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What does it look like?
Here and there; for both the woman and the כהן

phrases.english: This mole, what is the case?
phrases.notes: This is the mole the ברייתא in Step 13 listed as a blemish for women only.

phrases.english: If it has hair in it,
here and there it disqualifies.
If it does not have hair in it,
if it is a large mole,
here and there it disqualifies;
if it is a small mole,
here and there it does not disqualify,

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי שׁוּמָא הֵיכִי דָּמְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of sweat and turns to the next item in the ברייתא of Step 13, the mole.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that a mole is a blemish for a woman and not for a כהן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Every kind of mole gets the same ruling for women and כהנים, so no case is left where the two differ.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows the rules for moles
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports the breakdown: a mole with hair is a blemish, a large mole without hair is a blemish, and a small one is not. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says 'large' means the size of an Italian איסר.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: a mole with hair is a blemish. Without hair, a large one is a blemish and a small one is not. How big is large? רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said: the size of an Italian איסר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as the source for the breakdown it just gave about moles.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא is about blemishes in general. It is not limited to women, so its rules apply to כהנים too. That makes the question from Step 17 stronger: the rules are the same for everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: Italian איסר, a small coin used as a size measure
A תנא who gives the size for a 'large' mole

phrases.english: As it is taught:
A mole that has hair in it,
this is a blemish.
If it does not have hair in it,
a large one is a blemish;
a small one is not a blemish.
And what is large?
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel explained:
As large as an Italian issar.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: שׁוּמָא שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ שֵׂעָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the breakdown of moles in Step 17.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that each kind of mole gets the same ruling for women and כהנים
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on the laws of blemishes, with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's measure

steps.title: A small mole on her forehead
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא answers that the ברייתא means a small mole on a woman's forehead. Even though it is small, it is a blemish for her because of where it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: It is a mole on her forehead.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא answers the question about the mole. He says the ברייתא is talking about a mole on the forehead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A small mole usually does not count. On a woman's forehead, though, even a small one spoils her looks, so for her it is a blemish. This gives a case that counts for a woman and not for a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: In a case where it is located

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Hanina, said:
It is where it is positioned on her forehead.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא: בְּעוֹמֶדֶת עַל פַּדַּחְתָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the case by where the mole is
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No kind of mole counts for a woman but not for a כהן.
steps.terutzMaskana: A small mole on her forehead is a blemish for a woman.

steps.title: A mole on the forehead was already seen
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: a mole on her forehead is easy to see. The husband saw it and accepted it before the marriage, so he cannot complain about it later.
steps.simpleTranslation: On her forehead? He saw it and accepted it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's answer. A mole on the forehead cannot be a hidden blemish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blemish only helps the husband if he did not know about it when he married her. A forehead is out in the open, so he surely saw the mole and was fine with it. That makes the forehead case useless.

keyTerms.meaning: He saw it and accepted it

phrases.english: Her forehead?
It is something he saw and accepted!

steps.triggerLanguage: פַּדַּחְתָּהּ רָאָה וְנִיפַּיַּיס הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in Step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's case of a mole on the forehead
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A blemish in plain view was seen and accepted, so it cannot be grounds to complain.

steps.title: A mole under her head covering, sometimes seen
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the mole is under the cap on her head. Sometimes it shows and sometimes it does not, so the husband may never have seen it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: It is under the cap on her head. Sometimes it can be seen and sometimes it cannot.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא fixes the answer so it works. He moves the mole to a spot that is usually covered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the cap, the mole is still near the face and hurts her looks when it shows. Because it is often hidden, the husband may not have known about it. So it is a real blemish he can complain about.

keyTerms.meaning: The cap or covering on her head

steps.whatToRemember: A mole counts as a woman's blemish when it is small but sits under her head covering: it hurts her looks when it shows, and her husband may not have seen it.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:

phrases.aramaic: בְּעוֹמֶדֶת לָהּ תַּחַת כִּפָּה שֶׁל רֹאשָׁהּ,
phrases.english: It is where it is positioned under the cap of her head,
and sometimes it is seen
and sometimes it is not seen.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: בְּעוֹמֶדֶת לָהּ תַּחַת כִּפָּה שֶׁל רֹאשָׁהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 20 by moving the mole to a place that is sometimes hidden.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A forehead mole is always seen, so it cannot be a hidden blemish.
steps.terutzMaskana: A mole under her head covering is sometimes hidden, so the husband may not have seen it.

steps.title: A scar from a dog bite is a blemish
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says he heard from a great man, רבי שילא, that if a dog bit a woman and the bite left a scar, it is a blemish.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: I heard this from a great man, רבי שילא. If a dog bit her and the spot became a scar, that is a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a list of more blemishes for a woman. The first is a scar from a dog bite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds a new blemish that was not in the ברייתא. The wound itself heals, but the scar it leaves stays, and that scar counts as a blemish.

phrases.english: Rav Hisda said:

phrases.aramaic: הָא מִילְּתָא מִגַּבְרָא רַבָּה שְׁמִיעַ לִי,
phrases.english: I heard this matter from a great man,
and who is he? Rabbi Sheila:
If a dog bit her
and its place became a scar,
this is a blemish.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: הָא מִילְּתָא מִגַּבְרָא רַבָּה שְׁמִיעַ לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new list of extra blemishes for a woman after the mole discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A scar left by a dog bite is a blemish in a woman.

steps.title: A deep voice is a blemish in a woman
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says a deep voice in a woman is a blemish. He brings a פסוק that praises a sweet voice.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: A deep voice in a woman is a blemish, as it says: 'For your voice is sweet and your appearance pleasant.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא adds another blemish for a woman: a deep, heavy voice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts a sweet voice right next to good looks. That shows a woman's voice is part of what makes her pleasing, so a deep voice counts as a flaw.

phrases.english: Rav Hisda said:
A deep voice in a woman,
this is a blemish,
as it is stated: "For your voice is sweet and your appearance pleasant."
phrases.notes: שיר השירים 2:14

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: קוֹל עָבֶה בָּאִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second blemish added by רב חסדא, continuing the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A deep voice in a woman is a blemish, learned from the פסוק in שיר השירים.

steps.title: רבי נתן בירָאָה: a טפח between a woman's breasts
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן בירָאָה teaches a short ברייתא: 'Between a woman's breasts, a טפח.' He does not say whether this is good or bad, and the next steps argue about that.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נתן בירָאָה taught: Between a woman's breasts, a טפח.
steps.whatsHappening: A short ברייתא is quoted. It is not clear what it means, so it sets up the next steps, which try to explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives only a measure, a טפח, and no ruling. So we don't know yet whether a טפח is the ideal or a blemish. The following steps settle that.

keyTerms.meaning: A handbreadth, about four fingers wide

phrases.english: Rabbi Natan Bira'a taught:
Between a woman's breasts, a handbreadth.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַבִּי נָתָן בִּירָאָה: בֵּין דַּדֵּי אִשָּׁה טֶפַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another teaching about a woman's body to the list of blemishes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A measure of a טפח between a woman's breasts. What it means is decided in the next steps.

steps.title: רב אחא בריה דרבא: a טפח is a mark of beauty
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא wanted to explain, in front of רב אשי, that a טפח between the breasts is a good thing, a sign of beauty.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא, son of רבא, thought to say before רב אשי that a טפח is a good quality.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בריה דרבא offers a first reading of רבי נתן's ברייתא. He reads it as praise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the ברייתא as a description of the ideal woman. The word סבר, 'he thought,' hints that this reading will not hold up. רב אשי will reject it in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: He thought, he wanted to say
As a good quality, as praise

phrases.english: Rav Aha, son of Rava, thought
before Rav Ashi
to say that a handbreadth is a good quality.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָבַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first reading of the ברייתא from Step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A proposed reading: a טפח between the breasts is a mark of beauty.

steps.title: רב אשי: the ברייתא is about blemishes
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי tells רב אחא that the ברייתא appears in the list of blemishes. So a gap of a טפח is a blemish, not a mark of beauty.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to him: It was taught about blemishes.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי rejects רב אחא's reading. He says the ברייתא belongs with the blemishes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Where a teaching appears tells you what it means. Since this one is taught in the list of blemishes, a gap as wide as a טפח is a flaw.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to him:
It is taught with regard to blemishes,

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי: גַּבֵּי מוּמִין תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading of Step 25.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects all of רב אחא's reading of the ברייתא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: He ignored that the ברייתא is taught in the list of blemishes, not in praise of beauty.

steps.title: How wide is normal?
steps.stepSummary: If a טפח is a blemish, the גמרא asks how wide the normal gap is.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question. It sets up אביי's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once we know a טפח is too wide, we need to know what width is normal. Only then can we tell when the gap becomes a blemish.

phrases.english: And how much?
phrases.notes: The question is how wide the gap should normally be.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A follow-up question based on רב אשי's reading in Step 26.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The normal width between a woman's breasts

steps.title: אביי: three fingers
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the normal gap is three fingers wide. A טפח, which is four fingers, is too wide and counts as a blemish.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Three fingers.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question. He gives the normal width as three fingers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טפח is four fingers wide. If three fingers is normal, a gap of a טפח is clearly wider than normal. That fits רב אשי's reading that the ברייתא is listing a blemish.
steps.whatToRemember: Besides the blemishes that disqualify כהנים, a woman has extra blemishes: sweat that can be washed off, bad breath, a small mole in a sometimes-hidden spot, a dog-bite scar, a deep voice, and a gap of a טפח between her breasts, where three fingers is normal.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Three fingers.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: שָׁלֹשׁ אֶצְבָּעוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The normal gap is three fingers, so a טפח is a blemish.

steps.title: רבי נתן: breasts larger than normal are a blemish
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי נתן: a woman whose breasts are larger than other women's has a מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי נתן says, any woman whose breasts are larger than those of her friends, this is a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא from רבי נתן about another physical feature that counts as a blemish in a bride.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier ברייתא was about the gap between the breasts. This one is about the size of the breasts themselves. Being clearly larger than the normal size is listed as a מום.

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita: Rabbi Natan says:
Any woman whose breasts are large
compared with those of her friends,
this is a blemish.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי נָתָן אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second blemish rule from the same תנא after the discussion of the gap between the breasts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Breasts noticeably larger than the norm count as a מום.

steps.title: How much larger counts as a blemish?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how much larger than normal the breasts must be to count as a מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much larger?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a measurement. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Larger than her friends' is vague. A tiny difference cannot be a defect, so the גמרא wants a clear amount.

phrases.english: And how much?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the size limit in רבי נתן's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The size difference needed for the breasts to count as a blemish.

steps.title: The measure is a handbreadth
steps.stepSummary: רבי מיישא, quoting his grandfather רבי יהושע בן לוי, says the measure is a טפח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מיישא, the grandson of רבי יהושע בן לוי, said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי: a handbreadth.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer is given: breasts that are a טפח larger than normal count as a blemish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This turns רבי נתן's vague rule into a clear measurement. Anything less than a טפח larger is ordinary variation, not a מום.

keyTerms.meaning: Son of his son, a grandson

phrases.english: Rabbi Meyasha, the grandson
of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, said
in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi:
A handbreadth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי מְיָישָׁא בַּר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of how much.

steps.title: Can such a thing really happen?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא wonders whether breasts a whole טפח larger than normal actually exist.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is there really a case like this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions whether the case is realistic. This sets up a story in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טפח is a large difference. The גמרא checks that the rule describes something that really happens and is not just theory.

phrases.english: And is there such a case?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אִיכָּא כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether the measurement just given is realistic.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether breasts that large ever actually occur.

steps.title: רבה בר בר חנה's story of the Arab woman
steps.stepSummary: Yes. רבה בר בר חנה saw an Arab woman who threw her breasts over her shoulders and nursed her baby behind her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. As רבה בר בר חנה said: I saw a certain Arab woman who flung her breasts behind her and nursed her son.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that such cases exist and supports this with an eyewitness story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If breasts can be long enough to reach a baby on her back, then being a טפח larger than normal is certainly possible. So רבי יהושע בן לוי's measure describes a real situation.

phrases.aramaic: אִין, דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה:
phrases.english: Yes, as Rabba bar bar Chana said:
I saw a certain Arab woman
who flung her breasts behind her
and nursed her son.
phrases.notes: The baby was carried on her back, so she nursed him over her shoulder.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין, דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the doubt with an eyewitness report.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, such cases exist, as רבה בר בר חנה saw.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי נתן: breasts larger than normal are a מום. The measure is a טפח larger, and רבה בר בר חנה's story shows this really happens.

steps.title: Two kinds of children of Zion
steps.stepSummary: רבי מיישא reads the פסוק 'איש ואיש יולד בה' as including two people: the one born in ציון and the one who longs to see it.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And of Zion it shall be said: this man and that man were born in her, and the Most High shall establish her.' רבי מיישא, the grandson of רבי יהושע בן לוי, said: both the one born in her and the one who longs to see her.
steps.whatsHappening: Since רבי מיישא was just quoted, the גמרא brings another teaching of his. This one is about who counts as a true child of ציון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'איש ואיש,' 'man and man,' repeating the word. רבי מיישא reads this as two kinds of people: someone actually born in ארץ ישראל, and someone who longs to see it. Both are treated as children of ציון.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who looks forward, longs for

phrases.english: "And of Zion it shall be said:
phrases.notes: תהלים 87:5

phrases.english: this man and that man were born in her,
and the Most High shall establish her."

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי מְיָישָׁא בַּר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Meyasha, the grandson of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, said:
Both the one born in her
phrases.notes: The doubled words "man and man" are being read as two different people.

phrases.english: and the one who longs to see her.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְצִיּוֹן יֵאָמַר אִישׁ וְאִישׁ יוּלַּד בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new topic, linked only because it is taught by the same רבי מיישא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both the one born in ציון and the one who longs to see it count as its children.
steps.confusionAlert: This is a new topic, not part of the blemish discussion. It appears here only because רבי מיישא was quoted in step 31.

steps.title: אביי: one of them is worth two of us
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that one person of ארץ ישראל is worth two Babylonians.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: and one of them is worth two of us.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds his own comment to the praise of ציון: the people of ארץ ישראל are greater than the people of בבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי lived in בבל. 'Them' means the people of ארץ ישראל and 'us' means the Babylonians. He says the people born there are twice as great.

phrases.english: Abaye said: And one of them
phrases.notes: "Them" means people of ארץ ישראל; "us" means the Babylonians, אביי's own community.

phrases.english: is worth two of us.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: וְחַד מִינַּיְיהוּ עֲדִיף כִּתְרֵי מִינַּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the praise of the people of ציון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One native of ארץ ישראל is worth two Babylonians.

steps.title: רבא: a Babylonian who moves there is worth two of them
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that a Babylonian who goes up to ארץ ישראל is worth two of the people born there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: and one of us, when he goes up there, is worth two of them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds another level. A Babylonian who moves to ארץ ישראל becomes even greater than the people born there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי praised the natives of ארץ ישראל. רבא says that someone who comes from בבל and goes up there becomes greater still, worth two natives.

phrases.english: Rava said: And one of us,
when he goes up there,
is worth two of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: וְחַד מִינַּן כִּי סָלֵיק לְהָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on אביי's statement and adds the case of a Babylonian who moves to ארץ ישראל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Babylonian who goes up to ארץ ישראל is worth two natives there.

steps.title: Proof from רבי ירמיה
steps.stepSummary: In בבל, רבי ירמיה could not follow the Rabbis. After moving to ארץ ישראל, he was the one calling the Babylonians fools.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבי ירמיה, when he was here, did not know what the Rabbis were saying. When he went up there, he called us 'foolish Babylonians.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves רבא's claim with the example of רבי ירמיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In בבל, רבי ירמיה was a weak student. In ארץ ישראל he rose so high that he, rather than the native scholars, could criticize the Babylonians. This shows a Babylonian who goes up becomes even greater than the natives.

phrases.english: For Rabbi Yirmeya,
when he was here,

phrases.aramaic: לָא הֲוָה יָדַע מַאי קָאָמְרִי רַבָּנַן,
phrases.english: did not know what the Rabbis were saying;
when he went up there,
he calls us "foolish Babylonians."

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּהָא רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה דְּכִי הֲוָה הָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's claim with a real example.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that a Babylonian who goes up becomes greater than the natives.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רבי ירמיה, who went from a weak student in בבל to a critic of the Babylonians in ארץ ישראל.
steps.whatToRemember: Both the one born in ציון and the one who longs for it are its children. אביי praises the natives, and רבא says a Babylonian who goes up becomes greater still, as רבי ירמיה shows.

steps.title: New משנה: blemishes found while she is in her father's house
steps.stepSummary: If blemishes are found while the girl is still in her father's house, the father must prove they appeared after the אירוסין, which makes it the husband's bad luck.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If she had blemishes while still in her father's house, the father must bring proof that these blemishes appeared after she was betrothed, and so the husband's field was flooded.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It deals with a husband who finds blemishes in his betrothed while she still lives with her father, and says who must prove when they started.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the blemishes existed before the אירוסין, the husband was tricked and can cancel. If they appeared after, it is simply his bad luck, like a flood hitting his own field. Since the father is the one claiming the husband must still pay, the father has to bring the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: In her father's house, not yet married
His field was flooded, meaning it is his own bad luck

phrases.english: Mishnah:

phrases.aramaic: הָיוּ בָּהּ מוּמִין וְעוֹדָהּ בְּבֵית אָבִיהָ
phrases.english: If she had blemishes while she is still in her father's house,
the father must bring proof
that these blemishes came on her after she was betrothed,
and so his field was flooded.
phrases.notes: "His" means the husband's. Once she is betrothed to him, a new problem is his bad luck, like a flood on his land.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיוּ בָּהּ מוּמִין וְעוֹדָהּ בְּבֵית אָבִיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה about proving when a bride's blemishes began.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: While she is in her father's house, the father must prove the blemishes came after the אירוסין.
steps.whyThisMatters: The timing matters: blemishes from before the אירוסין make it a mistaken deal, while blemishes from after are the husband's loss.

steps.title: Blemishes found after she enters the husband's home
steps.stepSummary: Once she has entered the husband's home, the husband must prove the blemishes were there before the אירוסין, which would make it a mistaken deal. This is רבי מאיר's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she entered the husband's domain, the husband must bring proof that she had these blemishes before she was betrothed, and so his acquisition was a mistaken acquisition. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the opposite case: after the marriage, the burden of proof moves to the husband. It ends by naming רבי מאיר as the author.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now she lives in the husband's home and he wants to get out of paying, so he must prove. He must show the blemishes existed even before the אירוסין, because anything that began after the אירוסין is already his bad luck. Only then is it a מקח טעות.

keyTerms.meaning: A mistaken transaction, a deal that can be cancelled
These are the words of רבי מאיר

phrases.english: If she entered the husband's domain,
the husband must bring proof

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁעַד שֶׁלֹּא נִתְאָרְסָה הָיוּ בָּהּ מוּמִין אֵלּוּ,
phrases.english: that before she was betrothed she had these blemishes,
and so his acquisition was a mistaken acquisition.
phrases.notes: "His acquisition" is the marriage itself, which can be cancelled if he was misled.

phrases.english: These are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִכְנְסָה לִרְשׁוּת הַבַּעַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second case of the same משנה, where the burden moves to the husband.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After she enters the husband's home, the husband must prove the blemishes existed before the אירוסין in order to cancel.
steps.confusionAlert: The husband must prove the blemishes came before the אירוסין, not just before the wedding. A blemish that began between the אירוסין and the wedding is already his loss.

steps.title: The Rabbis begin to limit רבי מאיר's rule
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say this rule applies only to hidden blemishes.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the Rabbis say: in what case is this said? With regard to hidden blemishes.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים start to disagree with רבי מאיר by limiting when his rule applies. Their full view continues in the next part of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים say the husband's claim about blemishes applies only to hidden ones. The reason, that visible blemishes would have been noticed, is not stated yet and comes in the continuation of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case is this said?

phrases.english: But the Rabbis say:
In what case is this said?
With regard to hidden blemishes,

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the חכמים's dissent by narrowing רבי מאיר's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the חכמים, the claim of blemishes applies to hidden blemishes; the rest of their view follows.
